newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeri leader to visit Russia to discuss oil.
newsitem.headline: Azeri leader to visit Russia to discuss oil.

text.p: Azerbaijan's President Haydar Aliyev said on Wednesday he would visit Moscow on July 3 for an official state visit, and his country's oil wealth was likely to feature in his talks.
Aliyev told reporters before leaving on a trip to Uzbekistan that he hoped to discuss in Moscow the transit of oil from Azerbaijan through a pipeline to Russia's port at Novorossiisk.

"I received an invitation from President (Boris) Yeltsin to visit Moscow on July 3. This will be my first official visit to Russia and I think that during this visit we can discuss all the questions (related to oil transport)," he said.
It was not clear how long his visit would last.
Russia's state-owned oil pipeline monopoly has guaranteed that a pipeline linking Baku and Novorossiisk will be ready to take Azeri oil by October 1998.

The pipeline crosses the separatist-minded Russian region of Chechnya. Prime Minister Victor Chernomyrdin recently signed an agreement with the Chechen leadership on making repairs to the Chechen section of the route.
An $8 billion multinational consortium led by British Petroleum plc plans to use the route for early oil transport from three fields it is developing in the Azeri sector of the Caspian Sea.
Russia and Azerbaijan have had strained relations since the former Soviet republic gained independence in 1991, but Aliyev's planned visit is a further sign of a recent thaw.
